question.text:
Let $ \mathbf{T}: \begin{bmatrix} x\\ y\\ \end{bmatrix} \longrightarrow \begin{bmatrix} x^2+y^2\\ 2x+7y\\ \end{bmatrix}. $ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\mathbf{T}(k\mathbf{v})=k\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $\mathbf{v}$ and real scalar $k$
  2. $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_1+\mathbf{v}_2)=\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_1)+\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_2)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$
  3. $\mathbf{T}$ is NOT a linear transformation
question.explanation:
A linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ satisfies two properties:

\begin{align*} & \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}kx\\ky\end{bmatrix} = k \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}, \\[5pt] & \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_1+x_2\\y_1+y_2\end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\y_1\end{bmatrix} +\mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_2\\y_2\end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

  • Checking the first condition, we have

\begin{align*} \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} kx\\ ky\\ \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} (kx)^2+(ky)^2\\ 2(kx)+7(ky)\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} k^2(x^2+y^2)\\ k(2x+7y)\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= k\begin{bmatrix} k(x^2+y^2)\\ 2x+7y\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &\neq k \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x\\ y\\ \end{bmatrix}. \quad {\color{red} \times} \end{align*}

Therefore, $\textbf{T}$ is not a linear transformation.

  • Checking the second condition, we have

\begin{align*} \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1+x_2\\ y_1+y_2\\ \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} (x_1+x_2)^2 + (y_1+y_2)^2 \\ 2(x_1+x_2) + 7(y_1+y_2) \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} (x_1^2+y_1^2) + (x_2^2+y_2^2) + 2(x_1x_2+y_1y_2) \\ (2x_1+7y_1) + (2x_2+7y_2) \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} x_1^2+y_1^2 \\ 2x_1+7y_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} x_2^2+y_2^2 \\ 2x_2+7y_2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2(x_1x_2+y_1y_2) \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ y_1\\ \end{bmatrix} + \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_2\\ y_2\\ \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2(x_1x_2+y_1y_2) \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &\neq \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ y_1\\ \end{bmatrix} + \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_2\\ y_2\\ \end{bmatrix}. \quad {\color{red} \times} \end{align*}

As a result, only statement III is true.

question.text:
Let $ \mathbf{T}: \begin{bmatrix} x\\ y\\ \end{bmatrix} \longrightarrow \begin{bmatrix} x^2\\ 7y\\ \end{bmatrix}. $ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\mathbf{T}(k\mathbf{v})=k\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $\mathbf{v}$ and real scalar $k$
  2. $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_1+\mathbf{v}_2)=\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_1)+\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_2)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$
  3. $\mathbf{T}$ is NOT a linear transformation
question.explanation:
A linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ satisfies two properties:

\begin{align*} & \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}kx\\ky\end{bmatrix} = k \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}, \\[5pt] & \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_1+x_2\\y_1+y_2\end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\y_1\end{bmatrix} +\mathbf{T}\begin{bmatrix}x_2\\y_2\end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

  • Checking the first condition, we have

\begin{align*} \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} kx\\ ky\\ \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} (kx)^2\\ 7(ky)\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} k^2(x^2)\\ k(7y)\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= k\begin{bmatrix} k(x^2)\\ 7y\\ \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &\neq k \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x\\ y\\ \end{bmatrix}. \quad {\color{red} \times} \end{align*}

Therefore, $\textbf{T}$ is not a linear transformation.

  • Checking the second condition, we have

\begin{align*} \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1+x_2\\ y_1+y_2\\ \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} (x_1+x_2)^2 \\ 7(y_1+y_2) \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} x_1^2+ x_2^2 + 2x_1x_2 \\ 7y_1 + 7y_2 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} x_1^2 \\ 7y_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} x_2^2 \\ 7y_2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1x_2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] &= \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ y_1\\ \end{bmatrix} + \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_2\\ y_2\\ \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1x_2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &\neq \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ y_1\\ \end{bmatrix} + \mathbf{T} \begin{bmatrix} x_2\\ y_2\\ \end{bmatrix}. \quad {\color{red} \times} \end{align*}

As a result, only statement III is true.

question.text: Consider a linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}\,.$ If $\,\mathbf{v}_1 + \mathbf{v}_2=\mathbf{0}\,$ and $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_2)=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}\,$, find $\,\mathbf{T}(15\mathbf{v}_1+8\mathbf{v}_2).$
question.explanation:
First, we have that \begin{align*} 15\mathbf{v}_1+8\mathbf{v}_2 &= 15\mathbf{v}_1+15\mathbf{v}_2-7\mathbf{v}_2 \\[3pt] &= 15(\mathbf{v}_1+\mathbf{v}_2)-7\mathbf{v}_2 \\[3pt] &= 15(\mathbf{0})-7\mathbf{v}_2 \\[3pt] &= -7\mathbf{v}_2. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\[ \mathbf{T}(15\mathbf{v}_1+8\mathbf{v}_2) = \mathbf{T}(-7\mathbf{v}_2). \]

Now, since $\mathbf{T}$ is a linear transformation, we have that $\mathbf{T}(k\mathbf{v})=k\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$ So

\begin{align} \mathbf{T}(-7\mathbf{v}_2) &= -7\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}_2) \\[5pt] &= -7\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 21 \\ -7 \\ -49 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align}

In conclusion, $\mathbf{T}(15\mathbf{v}_1+8\mathbf{v}_2)=\begin{bmatrix} 21 \\ -7 \\ -49 \end{bmatrix}.$
